draft: Day 1: Arrive at Osaka, in the center of Japan's main Honshu island, and home to a bustling nightlife and many food options. In the morning, visit Osaka castle in the heart of the city, to experience the history of Japan's Edo period. In the afternoon, you can visit either Osaka aquarium Kaiyukan, once the largest aquarium in the world, or get tickets to go to Universal Studios Osaka, which has many themed attractions. At night, pay a visit to Dotonbori, Osaka's famous food alley with a variety of small bites and restaurants. Day 2: Visit Kyoto, Japan's cultural center and former capital. In the morning, visit the Fushimi Inari-taisha shrine, famous worldwide for its orange gates and trail that span almost 4 km. After the visit, explore the old town at the base of the shrine, and head over to Kiyomizu-dera, a famous Buddhist temple which offers stunning views and historical artifacts. In the afternoon and evening, pay a visit to downtown Kyoto, home to department stores and small yet delicious small restaurants. Day 3: Visit Hakone, a famed destination for its hot springs, Mt. Fuji views, and beautiful scenery. Spend some time to visit Lake Ashinoko to see a floating torii gate and expansive views of Mt. Fuji, Japan's tallest peak, visit the sulphur springs where the sulphur cooks chicken eggs so that they become black, then relax in the many hot springs around the region. Hakone is also known for its many ryokans, which are Japanese-style bed and breakfast inns often paired with hot spring onsens. Day 4-5: Spend the last two days in Tokyo, the heart of Japan and the most populated metropolitan area in the world. Tokyo offers many destinations, including the nightlife-heavy districts of Shinjuku and Roppongi, the shopping and fashion centers of Ginza and Harajuku, to the quirky and anime-filled area of Akihabara. Some famous attractions to hit in the city include the Senso-ji temple, Ueno park, Tokyo Skytree, Shibuya crossing, Tsukiji market, and the Imperial Palace.
instruction: Create a 5 day itinerary for a trip to Japan. Include visits to famous locations in Japan, and include a day-by-day breakdown of some activities to do and sites to visit.

draft: Public lands make up a huge proportion of the region between the crest of the Sierra Nevada and the Continental Divide in the Rockies, also known as the Intermountain West, and most of these lands are owned by the Federal government. Many residents of this sparsely populated region resent the control of these lands by distant bureaucrats whose regulations place significant restrictions on how the land is used. For this reason, movements have been ongoing for many years to work for the transfer of those lands to local authorities. While this sense of disenfranchisement is understandable, the truth is that local residents would suffer more from the loss of centralized management of these lands than they would gain through local control. This region is mostly desert, a landscape and ecosystem that is unusually vulnerable to degradation. Without the concerted efforts of an administration that can apply consistent regulation and stewardship of these lands across a broad territory that crosses state boundaries, the value of these lands to local residents would decline even further, becoming less productive and less attractive to the hunters, fishermen, and other tourists whose spending represents the majority of income for many of these Intermountain communities.
instruction: Write an argument for keeping public lands under federal control in the Intermountain West.

draft: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Kyle. Kyle owned a pet rabbit name Hip and loved it a lot. He would play with it a lot, feed it, have it hop around his room, and plenty of other things as well. One normal day, Kyle had to go to school and waved goodbye to Hip. Kyle left a can of soda next to Hip's cage, and Hip decided it wanted to try some. He ran to the side of the cage with the soda and crashed into it, knocking both the cage and the soda down. The door to the cage was open, and the imitation hay was spilled all across the room. The soda spilled across the room as well. Hip was able to get up just fine and he noticed the soda spill. Hip hopped over to the spill and started licking up the soda. Maybe it was his way of cleaning up his mess. But something started to change with Hip. Hip was feeling a little jittery. The caffeine in the can started to take effect, and Hip was hopping around the room a lot more than normal. He was moving twice as fast. The satisfaction from drinking the sugary drink made Hip hop twice as high! As high as the bed frame! Hip hopped on top of the bed and found a very cozy place to rest his legs. He didn't notice the rabbit feet markings on the covers or the ground. Hip was just happy he got to drink the soda. He tried jumping on the bed, and he found out that he could jump even higher on the bed! This was new territory for Hip! The feeling of being in the air for so long was refreshing, and Hip wanted to do it more. But Hip knew this wouldn't last. The mess that he made for Kyle was too much. The rabbit started to sulk and tire. All that jumping made him tired. He decided it was time to rest and recover. Hip had to wait for Kyle to clean up his mess. Either way, the experience that Hip had was amazing, and He will never forget it.
instruction: Can you write a short story about a rabbit drinking a can of soda for the first time? The sugar and caffeine would make it hop fast!

draft: No worries, dear! The Knockoff made me laugh, and I think you'll get a kick out of it for very different reasons. Authors Lucy Sykes and Jo Piazza describe the clash between a Gen X fashion magazine executive back from a six-month leave who discovers that her publication, Glossy, has been turned into an app. The main character, Imogen Tate, is cool and friends with everybody in the fashion world; whereas the 20-something leading the app project - Harvard MB Eve, Imogen's former assistant!- makes her young team of employees works all night and participate in stupid dances, before viciously firing them for trivial reasons. Imogen doesn't have the slightest clue about tech or apps (she's more of a Smythson notebook kind of person) but realizes that she has to learn a few things quickly before Eve destroys everything she has worked to build. No spoilers, but think of it as a sort of updated The Devil Wears Prada. It will make you laugh and might remind you of a few people you know.
instruction: Write a tl:dr review of this book review in the voice of a Gen X mom talking to her Gen Z daughter: Title: The Knockoff Author: Lucy Sykes and Jo Piazza ISBN: 9780385539586 No. of Pages: 352 Genre: Contemporary Fiction Origins: Doubleday Release Date: 19 May 2015 Synopsis: “An outrageously stylish, wickedly funny novel of fashion in the digital age, The Knockoff is the story of Imogen Tate, editor in chief of Glossy magazine, who finds her twentysomething former assistant Eve Morton plotting to knock Imogen off her pedestal, take over her job, and reduce the magazine, famous for its lavish 768-page September issue, into an app. When Imogen returns to work at Glossy after six months away, she can barely recognize her own magazine. Eve, fresh out of Harvard Business School, has fired “the gray hairs,” put the managing editor in a supply closet, stopped using the landlines, and hired a bevy of manicured and questionably attired underlings who text and tweet their way through meetings. Imogen, darling of the fashion world, may have Alexander Wang and Diane von Furstenberg on speed dial, but she can’t tell Facebook from Foursquare and once got her iPhone stuck in Japanese for two days. Under Eve’s reign, Glossy is rapidly becoming a digital sweatshop—hackathons rage all night, girls who sleep get fired, and “fun” means mandatory, company-wide coordinated dances to Beyoncé. Wildly out of her depth, Imogen faces a choice—pack up her Smythson notebooks and quit, or channel her inner geek and take on Eve to save both the magazine and her career. A glittering, uproarious, sharply drawn story filled with thinly veiled fashion personalities, The Knockoff is an insider’s look at the ever-changing world of fashion and a fabulous romp for our Internet-addicted age.” To say that the two clash is an understatement. Imogen struggles to learn the new rules of doing business to capitalize on the available technology, while Eve just wants Imogen out of the way. The dynamic between the two is fraught with tension and frustration and achingly realistic. Talk to anyone in management above a certain age, and they will all have stories similar to Imogen’s. Then again, talk to anyone Eve’s age and her frustrations are their frustrations. The Knockoff captures the individual sides perfectly. There is a lot to love in The Knockoff. Think of it as The Devil Wears Prada for the next generation. However, to expect the same story as Prada would be to seriously underestimate the twists and turns The Knockoff has in store for readers. Anyone who has ever been frustrated at work due to a genuine clash in personality and expectations should read The Knockoff. In fact, it would make a fantastic book club option, as it is quick, light, and humorous, and yet presents multiple situations and characters that are open to interpretation.

draft: Felicity was a soft-spoken librarian who enjoyed a quiet life with Felix, her ginger cat. When she wasn't working at the library, Felicity enjoyed cycling, bowling, and weekly meetings with the local book club. Her friends would describe her as soft-spoken and compassionate. However, shortly after her 32nd birthday, Felicity's life was turned upside down. Suddenly, objects started moving around on their own, seeming to come to her at the first thought of need. Even stranger, the weather seemed to reflect her moods perfectly. After a few days of odd happenings, Felicity turned to her trusty books to find an answer. Although she felt a bit ridiculous looking for books about magic and witchcraft as a rational, modern-day woman, it seemed to be her only option. Surely there must be some truth in the old tales. Finally, after weeks of searching, Felicity stumbled across a rare collection of 18th-century grimoires. These otherworldly tomes sent a shiver up her spine, but she knew that inside one of them lay the key to understanding why this was happening to her. When she brought home the stack of ancient books, Felicity set them down on her end table with a sigh. She couldn't fathom where to begin her search. Then, with a slight growl, Felix jumped up on the table, knocked the stack of books to the floor, walked straight to the one titled The Magus, and sat on the cover. It was almost as if he was trying to tell her something. With a shake of her head, Felicity picked up the book her cat seemed to have chosen, mumbling to herself that it was as good a place to start as any. But she couldn't shake the feeling that Felix was watching her expectantly for the rest of the evening.
instruction: Write the beginning of a short story about a 32-year-old female librarian named Felicity who has recently discovered she has magical powers. Describe her personality, physical appearance, and hobbies, including that she has an orange cat named Felix. Add that her powers include telekinesis and weather control.

draft: I am a pickle. Well, no that isn't quite right, I'm a cucumber right now but soon I will be a pickle. Days ago some friendly hands picked me up from my nice sunny patch in the field. I was about ready to come in, to be honest, the heat was getting to me and there were far too many rabbits lurking around. It was very nice to be carried inside, given a nice cool bath, and set aside for the night to sleep and relax. I woke up a bit later than usual still surrounded in the colander by my other cucumber friends. They were still sleeping so I did my best not to disturb them. They weren't a talkative bunch normally anyway. The sun was just starting to peak in through the curtains above the sink when a lady entered the room. The same lady who grabbed me from the patch yesterday. She seemed very friendly and nice. At least I thought so until she picked me up, bowl and all, and gave me a big shake. What a way to rise and shine. I could hear the other cucumbers grumbling too. She transported us a few feet away to another part of the countertop. Then, the lady mixed a bunch of ingredients in a big pot on the stove and it started to smell good but it also tickled my nose a bit. Perhaps a bit too garlicky for my tastes. Next thing I knew she was picking me up again but this time she stuck me in a jar! I couldn't believe it, it was finally happening! It's the most exciting day in any gherkins life. A few of my other cucumber friends joined me and we all nestled up close to each other. It was very cozy and everyone had a nice view through the glass too. Then, the nice lady gave us a warm bath. It felt even nicer than the cool bath I had before. It had hints of dill and pepper and it covered me from my tippy toes all the way to the top of my head. She put a nice little roof over top sealing me in. And I knew that from this day forward I was a cucumber no more, now I was one proud pickle.
instruction: Write a story from the perspective of a pickle as it is going from a cucumber in the field to being jarred and put away for the year.

draft: “What are you, the health inspector?” laughed Clay while brushing past the stranger who was giving him a dirty look. The disdain came from the fact the stranger, who indeed was the regional health inspector, determined there was no possibility Clay could have washed his hands between the brief moment when the toilet flushed and the doorknob turned. Clay was a cook at a small burger restaurant. For the most part, Clay was a decent worker, except he had a loud mouth and a short temper. An additional character flaw of Clay’s was not having the greatest sense of awareness about him. Maintaining this, he never saw his coworkers attempting to gain his attention via flailing arms. If he had given them his attention, they surely would have made certain Clay knew who he was talking to and, possibly, might have kept him from making any further mistakes. Since the attempt had failed, Clay continued his normal behavior. He returned to his grill station and produced his spatula from his rear pocket. The health inspector never saw him pick up any utensils, so Clay must have taken the spatula into the bathroom with him. Purely disgusted, the health inspector walked over to Clay’s station to continue his assessment. “If you want a burger,” Clay rolled his eyes and turned away, “you are going to have to put an order in up front. However, when you do that, make sure they tell me who it is for so I can prepare it special, just for you.” The health inspector, assuming Clay’s special burger was nothing anyone would want to consume, realized Clay was not fit to serve food to the public. Finally, the stranger pulled his wallet from a coat pocket and revealed his credentials. Clay could not believe it. In shock, his mouth stayed open long enough for a thin stream of drool to fall from his mouth and land on the cooktop. “I will be sure to include this in the report, too.” grinned the health inspector.
instruction: Write a funny tale about a terrible employee at a burger restaurant who gets caught slacking on the job and is delivered justice. Include notes of disgust in your writing, and make sure the employee (Clay) is unlikable.

draft: I sigh and drag my foot one more hateful step through the yellow grains, sores and bruises rioting painfully in my broken body. I lean desperately against my horse, and she whinnies. I know she hasn't much longer to live. The sun blazes in the sky, apathetic, and the wind carries sand into my face. My face throbs with pain as it wretchedly tries to cry tears to moisten my eyes, but there is no water to feed them. My battered, rusted, gritty armor glows with the twisting distortions of heat. But it is the girdle that is killing me. Worn from shoulder to waist as a baldric, the green girdle writhes like flickering emerald fire in the breeze. So airy and ephemeral, and yet the weight of it strains my tired soul. Under its burden, I fear I might buckle and collapse into the sand. My knees fail, and I plummet into the burning dune. My arms dig through the grains, and I try to hoist myself up by the reigns of my horse, but she falls too, without a sound, and lies still. I pull myself against her withered body, and the wind picks up, carrying a storm of sand into the air. I open my mouth and try to wail, but no words escape my parched throat. I lay, baking under the Arabian sun, and stare at the billowing girdle still alive in the wind, as though struggling to get away. I realize this is the end. With what remains of my strength, I tear my sword from its scabbard and slice the girdle from my body. It is carried away in the wind. Perhaps to the Grail, or perhaps to curse some other righteous fool. My sword slips out of my exhausted hand. As I die, I watch the flickering green cloth dance away into the desert.
instruction: Write a vignette about Sir Gawain. He is defeated and lost in the desert, on a quest for the grail. He is at the end of his journey, perishing in despair. His responsibility, symbolized by his green girdle, weighs on him. Write this in the first person.

It probably wasn’t horribly long in reality – years trapped in a dungeon are not kind to the legs – but I had at least escaped the Witch’s valley. Curling up by the gnarled roots of a blackened tree, my tears’ floodgates suddenly opened. I muffled my sobs as much as I could. “You should not dally, Miss.” I bolted upright at the voice. It was not the Witch’s screech, but a deep baritone. Even so, my heart trembled with fear. “Who’s there?!” A stag stepped out from the underbrush. It was not a tall one and was clearly advanced in years, but he looked me square in the eyes. “You cannot stay here. If you do not keep moving, the Witch’s minions will snatch you. Come.” Though skeptical, I had few options. I staggered to my feet and followed the greying stag deeper into the forest. The canopy blotted out all but the faintest glimmer of sunlight. I was nearly ready to collapse by the time he stopped. “You are safe for now. You may rest with us.” To my surprise, I saw the dim figures of many animals around me. Not only deer but squirrels, boars, rabbits, beavers, and more. They chittered amongst themselves excitedly. At length, the stag spoke again. “Did you truly escape the Witch’s Tower? Under your own power?” It took time to find my voice. “Yes,” I said meekly. “It took a long time of looking for opportunities.” “Then you may be the one who was foretold. The great champion who will be our avatar in the human world.” Suddenly the creatures draped a heavy cloak over my shoulders and an antlered helmet upon my head. “You will defend the forest from those who would do it harm and enlist the good peoples of the human world to battle evil. You, young lady, are the Thicket Warrior.”

draft: First of all, I am sorry to hear that you feel lonely and you should know that loneliness and isolation are widespread issues that you do not need to feel ashamed for. Unfortunately, the only way to form and retain friendships is to spend time with another person. If your work takes up a large amount of your waking time you will find it comparatively difficult to make friends with people outside of work. I am assuming that you are a man since men in particular form friendships around common interests. Are you sure that you don't share common interests with your coworkers? Ask about their interests and try to understand what they care about. Even if it turns out that you don't share common interests they will probably appreciate that you're trying to learn more about them. They may also feel the same way you do and want to form friendships with other people but simply not know how to make the first step. Good opportunities for casual conversation include lunch breaks and coffee/tea breaks. To find friends with shared interests in particular you can try to attend real-life events that revolve around said interests. You probably wouldn't feel comfortable at a rock concert with lots of people and loud music but how about something like Dungeons & Dragons where a small group of people plays a game in a quiet room? Maybe there are clubs for the discussion of books or anime that you could join. In any case, if you invest time and effort into making an activity fun for other people they will want to spend more time with you (but this of course requires time and effort). Finally, you mentioned that you don't have many friends - but this means that you still have some. Keep in touch with them and share what is happening in your lives with each other. Maintaining a friendship is much easier than forming a completely new one and you will feel more comfortable around people that you already know compared to strangers.

draft: There are several ways to improve Wi-Fi coverage in your home: Place your router in a central location: One of the most important things to consider when trying to improve your Wi-Fi coverage is the location of your router. Place your router in a central location in your home to ensure that the Wi-Fi signal can reach all areas of the house. Avoid placing the router in a corner or closet, as walls can weaken the signal and reduce the overall coverage. 1. Use a Wi-Fi extender: A Wi-Fi extender, also known as a range extender, can help extend the range of your Wi-Fi signal to reach areas of your home that are far from your router. Upgrade to a mesh network: If your home is larger, or if you have thick walls that are affecting your Wi-Fi signal, a mesh network system can provide better coverage. A mesh network consists of several small access points that are placed throughout your home and work together to provide a seamless Wi-Fi experience. 5. Update your Wi-Fi standard: If your router supports 802.11n or older standards, consider upgrading to a newer one, such as 802.11ac, which provides faster speeds and improved coverage.
